dashboard.visitorMixCaveat: Methodology: unique request_id values over the last 24h, with the full AccessLog aggregate as the denominator. Ordinary requests are recorded too, but normal requests retain only basic access fields and omit detailed request/response content. "Bot Visits" includes only requests the bot engine classifies as malicious or suspicious; known benign crawlers, such as search engines, count as human visits. "Unclassified Intercepts" are requests short-circuited by OWASP, CVE, ACL, or similar checks before bot detection; they have no bot score, so they are reported separately and do not count as human visits. The four categories sum to the persisted total; asynchronous queue drops, database write failures, and cache delay can create temporary gaps. If bot detection is disabled, Bot Visits remains 0.

dashboard.eventSparklineHint: Sparkline shows security-event count over the last {{hours}}h (all actions)
dashboard.visitorFusionCaption: Recorded HTTPS requests only: WAF did not terminate them and fusion evidence was sufficient; not a full-traffic ratio

stats.title: Runtime Stats
stats.caption: Counted since the scripts were loaded into the engine. A config reload recompiles them and resets the counters, so these are not historical totals.
stats.loadedScriptsHint: Scripts currently compiled into the engine. Disabled scripts are not loaded, and neither are enabled ones that failed to compile.
stats.runsHint: Total runs across all scripts, including the failed and timed-out ones.
stats.failuresHint: Deterministic defects such as handle() errors, panics or a missing entry function. Timeouts are counted separately.
stats.failureRateHint: Failures / runs. Failures are not jitter, so anything above 0.5% is worth investigating.
stats.timeoutsHint: Runs interrupted for exceeding the configured timeout. A timed-out run counts as no decision and never blocks the request.
stats.timeoutRateHint: Timeouts / runs. Read the ratio, not the absolute count: an isolated one or two come from GC pauses and CPU contention, and only a sustained ratio means the script is genuinely slow.
stats.avgHint: Average latency weighted by run count.
stats.avgSkewHint: The average covers every run including failures and timeouts, so a high timeout rate inflates it noticeably.
stats.lowSampleHint: Fewer than {{min}} runs, so the ratios carry little signal and no health verdict is applied.
stats.neverRunHint: The script is loaded but no request has triggered it since the last config reload.
stats.notLoadedHint: The engine holds no counters for this script: either the config has not reloaded yet, or the script failed to compile and was not loaded.
stats.disabledHint: Disabled scripts are not compiled into the engine, so they produce no runtime stats.
stats.unavailableHint: Runtime stats are unavailable, so this script's execution cannot be assessed.
stats.loadFailed: Runtime stats are temporarily unavailable. The scripts themselves are unaffected and keep making decisions.

stats.alertHint: The ratios below have crossed the threshold and are not isolated jitter. Review the script logic or raise its timeout.

dryRun.hint: Run the current source against a sample request. Nothing is saved and live config is untouched.
dryRun.headersHint: One per line as Name: value; {{count}} parsed.
dryRun.builtinHint: The two fields below simulate the built-in decision and are only readable by post-stage scripts.
dryRun.noDecisionHint: The script returned nil, so the request continues to later phases.
dryRun.iterationsHint: Number of repeated runs to test performance and stability
dryRun.kvUnavailableHint: Redis not configured, ctx.kv operations will return nil

help.contractIntro: The script must define a global handle(ctx); its return value decides the outcome:
help.returnNil: No decision; the request continues to later phases.
help.returnString: Used directly as the action name, e.g. "intercept".
help.returnTable: May carry action, message, redirect_to, status_code, headers and tags.
help.sandboxNote: The sandbox opens only base, table, string and math; load, require, getmetatable and print are removed, so scripts cannot touch the filesystem or the network.
help.actionsHint: Actions outside this list are ignored (treated as no decision) and never block a request by mistake.
help.ctxNote: ctx.headers uses lowercase keys; ctx.phase and ctx.action are only populated in the post stage and hold the built-in decision.
help.kvNote: With Redis configured the counters are shared across instances; otherwise available() returns false and the script should degrade rather than error. ctx.kv.incr ttl is measured in seconds, defaults to 300 when omitted, and must be an integer from 1 through 86400; invalid values fail that script execution.

rateLimit.title: Per-IP Rate Limit
rateLimit.description: Uses the shared KV store to limit each client IP to 100 requests per 60 seconds.

allowFalsePositive.title: Allow a Known False Positive

blockScanner.title: Block Known Scanners

jsPlugins.title: JavaScript Edge Scripts
jsPlugins.description: Manage site-scoped JavaScript edge script configuration.
jsPlugins.dialogDescription: Saved scripts enter the current snapshot through a configuration reload; request-stage scripts run after the original access-control, Basic Auth and inline OWASP checks, before the WAF pipeline, and the final access-control check runs again after mutations. Response-stage scripts transform the identity response entity (status, headers, body) before it is written.
jsPlugins.deleteConfirm: The script will stop taking effect and its source cannot be recovered. Continue?
jsPlugins.name: Script Name
jsPlugins.timeoutHint: Milliseconds; 0 uses the backend default, maximum {{max}}.
jsPlugins.enabledHint: Disabled scripts remain configured but are not processed at runtime.
jsPlugins.sourceHint: Export a default object with a fetch function that returns a mutation plan, or null/undefined for no changes. Request-stage scripts return a MutationPlan, response-stage scripts a ResponseMutationPlan. Source is limited to 256 KiB.
jsPlugins.dryRunSampleDescription: Request-stage field names must match RequestSnapshot; the response stage maps to ResponseSnapshot. headers and query_params are JSON objects whose values must be strings. request_id is fixed to dry-run and site_id is fixed to 0.
jsPlugins.dryRunJsonInvalid: {{field}} must be a JSON object with string values.
jsPlugins.runtimeDescription: QuickJS requires a build with CGO enabled and the quickjs build tag. stats always returns HTTP 200 with items and total; it reports only successfully compiled enabled scripts in the current snapshot, and an empty result can also mean that no snapshot is loaded. Counters are in memory and reset after reload.
jsPlugins.runtimeCompileErrors: {{count}} enabled script(s) currently failed snapshot compilation.
jsPlugins.statsSummary: {{total}} executable scripts loaded in the current snapshot
jsPlugins.statsEmpty: The stats response contains no currently loaded scripts. This can mean there are no successfully compiled enabled scripts, or that no snapshot is loaded; the empty response alone does not identify a runtime failure.

help.contractDescription: Both stages use an ES module default export object with fetch(snapshot, env, ctx). QuickJS is available only in builds with CGO enabled and the quickjs build tag; this panel does not add Lua action, tags or KV semantics.
help.requestStage: Request-stage scripts run by priority and ID after the original access-control, Basic Auth and inline OWASP checks, before the WAF pipeline; after a mutation, final access control is checked again.
help.responseStage: Response-stage scripts run by priority and ID before the identity response entity is written and may only mutate status, headers and body; streaming (SSE/WebSocket) paths are not affected. Scripts return a ResponseMutationPlan.
help.snapshotDescription: Scripts read a read-only request snapshot; it is not a MutationPlan that can be returned directly.
help.mutationDescription: Request-stage scripts should return only these request mutation fields; a missing field means no change, while an empty string explicitly replaces with empty.
help.mutationSemantics: Request-stage return {} means successful execution with no request changes; dry-run result: {} is also a successful empty plan. Returning the request snapshot or any unknown field is an error; path, raw_query, headers and body are checked for length, control characters and forbidden headers by the backend.
help.responseMutationDescription: Response-stage scripts must return only status, body, set_headers and delete_headers; a missing field means no change. body is limited to 16 KiB, status must be within 100-999, and header edits follow the MutationPlan forbidden-header and size checks.
help.limitsDescription: These limits come from the backend MutationPlan and RequestSnapshot/ResponseSnapshot validators; an over-limit error may be returned in the error field of an HTTP 200 response.
help.pathLimit: path: must start with one / and not //; it cannot contain ?, #, CR, LF, or other control characters, be an absolute URI, or carry a query/fragment; each field is limited to 16 KiB.
help.rawQueryLimit: raw_query: cannot contain #, CR, or LF and must be accepted by url.ParseQuery; each field is limited to 16 KiB.
help.methodBodyLimit: method must be an HTTP token; each method, body, path, and raw_query mutation string is limited to 16 KiB.
help.headerLimit: set_headers and delete_headers allow at most 128 entries each; names must be HTTP tokens; host, content-length, transfer-encoding, connection, upgrade, proxy-connection, and trailer are forbidden; names and values are each limited to 8 KiB, values cannot contain control characters or CR/LF, and one mutation cannot set and delete the same header.
help.snapshotLimit: Source is limited to 256 KiB. Live inspection truncates both request and response snapshot bodies at 48 KiB; dry-run rejects a sample body over 48 KiB. headers allow 256 entries each; snapshot scalars, keys, and values are limited to 16 KiB each; serialized snapshots to 128 KiB.
help.sampleDescription: You can provide method, path, raw_query, host, client_ip, user_agent, content_type, body, headers and query_params. request_id and site_id are fixed by the backend and are not form fields.
help.scopeDescription: A global script applies to all matching sites; a bound script applies only to that site.
help.siteIdDescription: Selecting global during edit explicitly submits null and clears the previous site scope.
help.runtimeDescription: validate and dry-run return HTTP 503 when QuickJS is unavailable; stats returns HTTP 200 with an empty items array when its holder is unavailable. Dry-run compile errors return HTTP 200 with error and result:null but no execution_time_ms; execution and mutation-validation errors return HTTP 200 with error, result:null and execution_time_ms. Stats are in-memory counters for the current snapshot and reset after reload.
help.failureDescription: fail_open skips the script after execution or mutation-validation failure and continues; request-stage fail_closed makes the data plane return HTTP 503, and response-stage fail_closed fails response writing (502).

skipPathByPhase.description: Requests matching a path skip the selected phase; unconfigured phases continue normally.
skipPathByPhase.emptyPhase: No skipped paths are configured for this phase.
skipPathByPhase.validationFailed: Remove empty paths or enter a non-empty path for every item.
skipPathByPhase.inheritHint: Keep null so this site inherits the global mapping.
skipPathByPhase.overrideHint: An empty map explicitly skips nothing; a non-empty map replaces the global configuration.
